name: tui-vpn
tagline: WireGuard and its control plane, from the terminal
description:
WireGuard from the terminal, together with the self-hosted control plane that decides who is allowed onto it.

The status screen reads your interfaces straight from `wg show all dump`: peers, endpoints, handshakes, transfer, allowed IPs and keepalive. Every change, from creating an interface to adding a peer, is previewed as the exact command line and applied only after you confirm it. A private key is never shown, typed, or put on a command line.

With a [Headscale](https://headscale.net) control plane it also manages users, nodes and pre-auth keys, and configures the server itself: `S` sets how clients reach it (plain http, Let's Encrypt, an own certificate or a reverse proxy, plus the MagicDNS domain), `O` writes the `oidc` section, each as a minimal diff of `/etc/headscale/config.yaml` followed by a restart, or the enable a disabled unit needs. `F` fixes state files the service account does not own. The OIDC client secret is typed masked, written mode 600 to its own file, and never displayed again.

Run it with `--demo` to see every screen with nothing installed.

screenshots.caption: The status screen: WireGuard interfaces, their state and peer counts, read from wg
The peers screen: endpoints, handshake age and transfer for the selected interface
The users screen under the control-plane panel: unit state, file ownership, transport, base domain, redirect URI, the IdP, and that a secret is set
The Headscale nodes screen: who owns each node and its state, above the OIDC identity note
The help screen: keys, and how identity works over OIDC

keys.action: Switch screen (interfaces, peers, users, nodes, keys)
Create a new interface from zero (keygen, conf, optional up)
Bring the selected interface up / down
Save the interface's runtime config (wg-quick save)
Add / remove a peer on the interface (add: optional pre-shared key file)
Create a Headscale user (users screen) or pre-auth key (keys screen)
Control plane (users screen): server and transport / OIDC provider (Google, generic)
Fix ownership of headscale's state, secret and backup files (users screen)
Expire / rename / delete the selected node

notes.impact: `preauthkeys list` requires a `--user`, so the pre-auth keys screen may be empty; users and nodes are unaffected

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn
cd tui-vpn && make demo

pacman.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

apt.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

dnf.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn/releases/download/v{version}/tui-vpn_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-vpn
sudo install -m0755 tui-vpn /usr/local/bin/tui-vpn
binary.note: Available once the first release is tagged.

security.needs_sudo: Reading WireGuard needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, the Headscale CLI talks to a root-owned socket, and config.yaml and headscale's state directory are root-only, so those reads escalate; `ip link` and `systemctl is-active` do not. Every mutation escalates, previewed and confirmed first.
security.no_network_note: On demand only: configuring an identity provider (or --check --probe-issuer) fetches the issuer's public /.well-known/openid-configuration with curl to check the URL. Read-only, unprivileged; a failure is a warning, not a refusal. Nothing else leaves the machine.
